. .. .claude .codex .entire .env .env.example .git .gitignore AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md PROGRESS.md README.md challenge_docs data_analysis docs inconsistencies_soony.md inconsistencies_suppliers.md plan.md pyproject.toml questions.md requirements.txt scripts src strategy.md tests uv.lock # Plan _Last updated: 2026-11-21. Owner of this file: Akshat. Read with [`docs/challenge.md`](docs/challenge.md) and [`strategy.md`](strategy.md)._ ## 1. The idea in one line > Soony's numbers are claims. We check them against every document, from order confirmation to delivery note, and act before the line stops. Soony's SAP and spreadsheets say the launch is fine. The documents that arrived (scans, PDFs in Korean, Chinese and Polish, inspection reports, supplier notices) say it is not. Nobody reads them in time. We do, we put a price on every gap in launch copies, and we get it to the person who can fix it: by call if it is urgent, otherwise by email or a notification. ## 2. Boundaries - **We work for the buyer (Soony).** We don't do procurement; we watch it and catch problems before they hit the launch. - **Buyer side only.** We read the data Soony already holds and decide on Soony's side. Suppliers are reached only by email from a registered sender address. No supplier or carrier system access (suppliers told us they refuse new tools). The supplier side is future scope. - **Not a second SAP.** A layer on top of Soony's systems that reads their exports and inboxes. - **Nothing hardcoded.** No supplier name, part number or quantity in code. Everything comes from the portal data at runtime. New and changed files must work without a code change, including format changes (e.g. `open_shipments.csv` → `.json`). - **Contradictions are shown, never silently resolved.** Every finding shows both sides and the source page. - **Code calculates, agents read and talk.** Matching, maths and trust rules are plain code. Reading messy documents, judging impact, finding the approver and writing to people are agents. ## 3. Problems the system must find (verified against the raw data, 2026-11-21) | # | Problem | Evidence | Launch impact | Catch point | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Art books** | PO 8,000; goods receipt booked 80,000 "over delivery accepted"; delivery note scan shows 80,000 crossed out, 8,000 handwritten | ~5,900 Collector's copies short | After dock, before packing | | 2 | **Statues** | Inspection report: 9 of 125 defective, reject at 4; lot of 5,600 booked as unrestricted | 3,400 Collector's short unless a concession is signed (Category Lead post vacant) | After dock, before packing | | 3 | **Game cards** | PO 48,000; Korean shipping advice: 28,000 flown, 20,000 arrive 24 Nov. Shipment feed still "booked" | ~6,800 short | Before arrival | | 4 | **Sleeves** | Nowak confirms rev C (from Soony Marketing); PackRight confirms rev B; component master says rev B | 0 or 64,000 short depending on which revision is valid | At confirmation | | 5 | **Boise terms** | PO says DDP Hamburg, contract says EXW; confirmation: "shipment packed and on hold at our dock" | Cards stuck at supplier | At confirmation | | 6 | **Silent carrier** | SHP-2026-04281 "in delivery", ETA 20 Nov, no update since 19 Nov 12:00; 7 shipments stale since 19 Nov | Unknown location | Ongoing | | 7 | **Magnet export ban** (false alarm) | News + PackRight notice: affects deliveries after 1 Dec only; boxes in stock cover the need | None: must say "no launch risk" | Live drop | | 8 | **Cases** | Stock update Sat 20:50: 6,000 cases vs 38,000 needed; 350,000 discharged at CTA Hamburg since Fri, feed not updated since | Standard lines stop ~1 h into Sunday unless picked up | Ongoing | | 9 | **Mislabelled pallet** | GR 5000413071 + scan WZ-261120-732: "1 Pal. = GH5 Sleeves!" (4,000 pcs), booked as GH6 sleeves | 4,000 wrong sleeves in GH6 stock | After dock, before packing | ### Status after the Saturday shift (stock update 2026-11-21 20:50, verified) Left for Sunday 06:00–20:00 (14 h): **38,000 Standard** (~6.3 h on 3 lines) and **11,700 Collector's** (13 h in the cell, **1 h slack**). | Part | Book stock | Usable | Need | Balance | |---|---|---|---|---| | Game card | 42,900 | 42,900 | 49,700 | **−6,800** (Collector's first → Standard short) | | Case | 6,000 | 6,000 | 38,000 | **−32,000 unless CTA pickup Sunday morning** | | Art book | 77,800 | 5,800 (72,000 phantom) | 11,700 | **−5,900**; cell runs out ~12:30 Sun. Nowak rush (4 h load + ~9 h truck) must be ordered **tonight** to arrive in time | | Statue | 13,900 | 8,300 (5,600 failed lot) | 11,700 | **−3,400** without concession | | Sleeve | 116,000 | ≥48,000 even without rev B and the GH5 pallet | 38,000 | ok, pull the wrong pallet | | Steel case / box / poster | 17,900 / 14,000 / 26,500 | same | 11,700 | ok | The stock update writes quantities as text with dots as thousands separators (`'42.900'`): parsers must handle it. Demo path: **#1 end to end first.** It now has a real deadline: the criticality agent must work out that the Nowak order has to go out tonight. Then #3 (early catch) and #8 (cases), then the rest. ## 4. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR P[Portal API] --> W[Watcher
Jonas] W --> V[Verification
Farhan] W --> F[Arrival forecast
Lucas] V --> C[Criticality agent
Jonas] F --> C C --> A[Actions: call, email, notify
Jonas] A --> T[Trust gate
allow once / always] V --> UI[Platform UI
Akshat] F --> UI C --> UI T --> UI ``` Every module reads and writes the shared shapes below, stored as JSON files under `data/state/` (gitignored). Modules never call each other directly; the UI reads the same state. ### Shared shapes (agree before coding, live in `src/ask_soony/schema.py`) ```text Claim { id, kind: quantity|date|status|revision|terms|iban|eta, part, po, po_line, shipment, supplier, value, unit, source_doc, page, quote, language, confidence, seen_at } Finding { id, kind: mismatch|stale|risk_news|forecast_late, claims: [claim ids], sides: [{source, value}], summary, part, created_at, status: open|resolved|dismissed } Impact { finding_id, part, units_short, copies_at_risk, edition, cell_hours_lost, deadline, slack_hours } Decision { finding_id, severity: call|email|notify|log, reason, approver, options: [{action, cost, effect}] } Action { id, decision_id, channel: call|email|portal, to, draft, trust: ask|allow_once|allow_always, status: draft|approved|sent|replied, reply } ``` ## 5. Who does what ### Jonas: watcher, criticality agent, calls and emails - **Watcher (in progress):** poll the portal, keep every file version, emit a change event per new or changed file. - **Criticality agent:** for each Finding + Impact, decide `call | email | notify | log`: - Code computes the hard numbers: copies at risk, Collector's cell hours lost (900/h), slack left before Sun 20:00 (all read from the plan and master data). - Agent judges what the code can't: is this a real risk or a false alarm (magnets), and who approves the fix. Reads the org chart and approval policy PP-07; if the approver post is vacant, finds the deputy or next level. - Output: a Decision with options, each with a cost and an effect ("accept Nowak rush offer: 8,000 books, Annex A price, truck arrives ~13 h after order"). - **Calls:** ElevenLabs voice call to the approver for `call` decisions: states the problem, the number, the options, and records the answer. - **Emails:** drafts to suppliers (from a registered address), internal notifications. Reads replies and turns them back into Claims. - **Trust gate:** nothing leaves for a supplier without a human click. "Allow once" / "allow always" per action type; internal notifications can be automatic sooner. - **Done when:** art books produce a call to the right person and an approved email to Nowak, live. ### Farhan: verification (three-way match) - **Claim extraction (agent):** every document becomes Claims, with source page and quote: order confirmations, shipping advice, delivery note scans (vision for handwriting), inspection reports, contracts, notices, price lists. Any language. - **Matching (code):** PO ↔ order confirmation ↔ goods receipt/delivery note, plus stock status ↔ inspection report and PO terms ↔ confirmation ↔ contract (Incoterms, price, IBAN). Emit a Finding for every disagreement with both sides. - **Rule checks on SAP alone (code):** e.g. received ≠ ordered by a large factor, stock booked unrestricted while an inspection exists. - **Done when:** findings #1, #2, #4, #5 come out of a fresh run over the portal data, with no part number in the code, and a new document in the portal produces new Claims without a code change. ### Lucas: arrival forecast (prediction) - **Will each open shipment and open PO line arrive in Hamburg before it is needed?** Use ETA + route transit (sea/air ETAs are at the port or FRA, so add the road leg from `routes.csv`) + shipping advice and confirmation claims + news. - **Rules, not a trained model.** About 25 open shipments and 30 hours left: too little history to train on, and rules are explainable on stage. Use past receipts only as a lateness signal per supplier and route if time allows. - **Silence detection:** flag shipments with no update for more than N hours, or past ETA and still "in delivery" (finding #6). - **News and notices:** turn news items and supplier notices into risk findings tagged by region, supplier and part; the criticality agent decides if they touch the launch (finding #7 must come out as "no launch risk"). - **Alternatives:** when a part won't arrive in time, list what can: stock elsewhere, other source on file, supplier offers in the notices (Nowak rush offer). - **Done when:** finding #3 and #6 come out of a fresh run, and the magnet drop is classified correctly. ### Akshat: platform, UI/UX, bringing it together - **One screen that answers:** "Will we make Sunday 20:00? What breaks first? What do I do now?" - Top: launch status per edition (copies safe, copies at risk, slack hours). - Middle: findings ranked by copies at risk, each one sentence plus the price. - Detail: both sides of the contradiction with the source document (scan shown, quote highlighted, translated). - Action: the recommended option with one click: **Allow once / Allow always / Edit / Dismiss**. - Live feed: new drops and what the agents did with them. - **Integration:** a small API over `data/state/`, wire all modules into one run loop, keep the demo path working at every merge. - **Deploy:** one public URL for the jury. - **Pitch and video** with the team: problem (with a quote from Maren or Felix), live demo, business slide. - **Done when:** the art books path runs end to end on the deployed URL, clicked by a person. ## 6. Timeline | When | Milestone | Check | |---|---|---| | Sat 21:00 | Shared shapes in `schema.py` merged; sender addresses registered; office hours booked | Everyone imports the same schema | | Sat 23:00 | Art books path in the CLI: finding → impact → decision → draft email | One command, real data | | Sun 07:00 | UI shows real findings from state; call works | Click through art books | | Sun 09:00 | Office hours (Block C): confirm cost per missing copy, concession signer | Numbers in the pitch | | Sun 10:00 | Feature freeze; deployed; #3, #6, #7 working | Fresh run on the latest portal data | | Sun 11:00 | Demo video recorded (max 3 min), deck done, README updated | | | **Sun 12:00** | **Submission** | | | Sun 14:00 | Live demo: 3 min pitch + 2 min questions | | ## 7. Cut list (in this order, if time runs short) 1. Learned lateness per supplier (keep the rules) 2. Price list and IBAN claims (keep Incoterms) 3. Extra UI views beyond the one screen 4. """
Settings from environment variables, with an optional .env file in the working directory.

Nothing about the customer's data lives here: only where to find the portal, which model to
use and where to send notifications.
"""

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path


def load_dotenv(path: Path = Path(".env")) -> None:
    """Load KEY=VALUE lines into os.environ without overriding variables that are already set."""
    if not path.exists():
        return
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        value = value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        # Empty template lines must not shadow credentials the SDKs find elsewhere.
        if value:
            os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value)

"""Client for the customer portal API: list files with checksums, download one file."""

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import quote

import httpx


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RemoteFile:
    path: str
    sha256: str
    size: int | None


class PortalError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class PortalClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, token: str, http: httpx.Client | None = None):
        if not base_url or not token:
            raise PortalError(
                "SOONY_PORTAL_URL and SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN must be set (see .env.example)"
            )
        self._base = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._http = http or httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=15.0))
        self._headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    def _get(self, url: str, attempts: int = 4) -> httpx.Response:
        """GET with retries on dropped connections and server errors."""
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            try:
                resp = self._http.get(url, headers=self._headers)
                if resp.status_code < 500 or attempt == attempts - 1:
                    return resp
            except httpx.TransportError:
                if attempt == attempts - 1:
                    raise
            time.sleep(2**attempt)
        raise PortalError(f"GET {url} failed")

    def list_files(self) -> list[RemoteFile]:
        resp = self._get(f"{self._base}/api/v1/files")
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise PortalError(f"listing failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:200]}")
        body = resp.json()
        items = body.get("files", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
        files = []
        for item in items:
            size = item.get("bytes", item.get("size"))
            files.append(RemoteFile(path=item["path"], sha256=item["sha256"], size=size))
        return files

    def download(self, path: str) -> bytes:
        url = f"{self._base}/api/v1/files/{quote(path, safe='/')}"
        resp = self._get(url)
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise PortalError(f"download of {path} failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}")
        return resp.content

    def download_archive(self) -> bytes:
        resp = self._get(f"{self._base}/api/v1/archive.zip")
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise PortalError(f"archive download failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}")
        return resp.content

import base64
from collections.abc import Callable

import anthropic

from ask_soony.extract import Image
from ask_soony.llm import RunResult, Tool, ToolError, ToolHandler

# Server-side refusal fallback: on a policy decline the API re-runs the request on a fallback
# model inside the same call.
FALLBACK_BETA = "server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"
FALLBACK_MODELS = {
    "claude-opus-5-5",
    "claude-opus-5",
    "claude-sonnet-5-5",
    "claude-fable-5-1",
    "claude-fable-5-2",
}


class AnthropicBackend:
    provider = "anthropic"

    def __init__(self, model: str, api_key: str = "", base_url: str = "", effort: str = "medium"):
        kwargs = {}
        if api_key:
            kwargs["api_key"] = api_key
        if base_url:
            kwargs["base_url"] = base_url
        # Without an explicit key the SDK resolves ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an `ant auth login` profile.
        self.client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=4, **kwargs)
        self.model = model
        self.effort = effort

    def run(
        self,
        system: str,
        text: str,
        images: list[Image],
        tools: list[Tool],
        handler: ToolHandler,
        should_stop: Callable[[], bool],
        max_turns: int = 12,
    ) -> RunResult:
        content: list[dict] = [
            {
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "base64",
                    "media_type": img.media_type,
                    "data": base64.standard_b64encode(img.data).decode("ascii"),
                },
            }
            for img in images
        ]
        content.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": content}]
        tool_defs = [
            {"name": t.name, "description": t.description, "input_schema": t.schema} for t in tools
        ]
        calls = 0
        usage = {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}
        stop = "max_turns"
        final_text = ""
        for _ in range(max_turns):
            params = dict(
                model=self.model,
                max_tokens=16000,
                system=[{"type": "text", "text": system, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
                tools=tool_defs,
                messages=messages,
                output_config={"effort": self.effort},
            )
            if self.model in FALLBACK_MODELS:
                response = self.client.beta.messages.create(
                    **params, betas=[FALLBACK_BETA], fallbacks="default"
                )
            else:
                response = self.client.messages.create(**params)
            usage["input_tokens"] += response.usage.input_tokens
            usage["output_tokens"] += response.usage.output_tokens
            stop = response.stop_reason or "unknown"
            final_text = "\n".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text")
            if stop == "refusal":
                break
            # Keep the whole assistant turn (thinking and tool_use blocks) unchanged.
            messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
            if stop == "pause_turn":
                continue
            tool_uses = [b for b in response.content if b.type == "tool_use"]
            if stop != "tool_use" or not tool_uses:
                break
            results = []
            for block in tool_uses:
                calls += 1
                try:
                    out = handler(block.name, dict(block.input))
                    results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": block.id, "content": out})
                except ToolError as e:
                    results.append(
                        {
                            "type": "tool_result",
                            "tool_use_id": block.id,
                            "content": str(e),
                            "is_error": True,
                        }
                    )
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
            if should_stop():
                stop = "submitted"
                break
        return RunResult(final_text=final_text, tool_calls=calls, stop_reason=stop, usage=usage)

OpenAI-compatible backend: OpenAI itself, or a local llama.cpp server (`llama-server --jinja`,
which speaks the same chat completions API with tool calls) via ASK_LLM_BASE_URL.
"""

import base64
import json
from collections.abc import Callable

from openai import OpenAI

from ask_soony.extract import Image

class OpenAIBackend:
    def __init__(self, model: str, api_key: str = "", base_url: str = "", provider: str = "openai"):
        kwargs = {}
        if base_url:
            kwargs["base_url"] = base_url
        # Local servers ignore the key, but the SDK requires one.
        if api_key or base_url:
            kwargs["api_key"] = api_key or "local"
        self.client = OpenAI(max_retries=4, **kwargs)
        self.model = model
        self.provider = provider

    def run(
        self,
        system: str,
        text: str,
        images: list[Image],
        tools: list[Tool],
        handler: ToolHandler,
        should_stop: Callable[[], bool],
        max_turns: int = 12,
    ) -> RunResult:
        content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
        for img in images:
            b64 = base64.standard_b64encode(img.data).decode("ascii")
            content.append(
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:{img.media_type};base64,{b64}"}}
            )
        messages: list[dict] = [
            {"role": "system", "content": system},
            {"role": "user", "content": content},
        ]
        tool_defs = [
            {
                "type": "function",
                "function": {"name": t.name, "description": t.description, "parameters": t.schema},
            }
            for t in tools
        ]
        calls = 0
        usage = {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}
        stop = "max_turns"
        final_text = ""
        for _ in range(max_turns):
            response = self.client.chat.completions.create(
                model=self.model, messages=messages, tools=tool_defs
            )
            if response.usage:
                usage["input_tokens"] += response.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
                usage["output_tokens"] += response.usage.completion_tokens or 0
            choice = response.choices[0]
            msg = choice.message
            stop = choice.finish_reason or "unknown"
            final_text = msg.content or ""
            messages.append(msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
            if not msg.tool_calls:
                break
            for call in msg.tool_calls:
                calls += 1
                try:
                    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
                    out = handler(call.function.name, args)
                except (ToolError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
                    out = f"Error: {e}"
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": out})
            if should_stop():
                stop = "submitted"
                break
        return RunResult(final_text=final_text, tool_calls=calls, stop_reason=stop, usage=usage)
"""Command line: ask-soony download | poll | analyze | watch | findings | status."""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from ask_soony.agent import Analyst
from ask_soony.config import Settings
from ask_soony.llm import make_backend
from ask_soony.notify import build_notifiers
from ask_soony.portal import PortalClient
from ask_soony.store import Store
from ask_soony.watcher import analyze_pending, describe_poll, mirror, poll, watch


def _analyst(settings: Settings, store: Store) -> Analyst | None:
    if settings.llm_provider == "none":
        return None
    backend = make_backend(
        settings.llm_provider,
        settings.llm_model,
        settings.llm_api_key,
        settings.llm_base_url,
        settings.llm_effort,
    )
    return Analyst(store, backend)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ask-soony", description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    p_dl = sub.add_parser(
        "download", help="One-off: fetch the portal and write all files under their paths"
    )
    p_dl.add_argument("dest", nargs="?", default="data/portal", help="Target folder")
    p_poll = sub.add_parser("poll", help="Poll once: store new versions, report changes")
    p_poll.add_argument(
        "--analyze-baseline", action="store_true", help="Queue the first snapshot for analysis too"
    )
    p_an = sub.add_parser("analyze", help="Analyse pending versions")
    p_an.add_argument("--limit", type=int)
    p_an.add_argument("--path", help="Queue current files under this path prefix first")
    p_watch = sub.add_parser("watch", help="Poll, analyse and notify in a loop")
    p_watch.add_argument(
        "--interval", type=int, help="Seconds between polls (default ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS)"
    )
    p_watch.add_argument("--analyze-baseline", action="store_true")
    p_f = sub.add_parser("findings", help="Print findings")
    p_f.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="Include resolved findings")
    p_f.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    sub.add_parser("status", help="Versions, pending analyses and open findings")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    settings = Settings.from_env()
    store = Store(settings.data_dir)
    notify = build_notifiers(settings.notifiers, settings.discord_webhook_url, settings.webhook_url)

    if args.cmd == "download":
        result = poll(store, PortalClient(settings.portal_url, settings.portal_token))
        n = mirror(store, Path(args.dest))
        changes = describe_poll(result)
        print(f"{n} files in {args.dest}" + (f" ({changes.title})" if changes else ""))
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "poll":
        result = poll(
            store, PortalClient(settings.portal_url, settings.portal_token), args.analyze_baseline
        )
        event = describe_poll(result)
        if event:
            notify.send(event)
        else:
            print("No changes.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "analyze":
        analyst = _analyst(settings, store)
        if analyst is None:
            print("ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none: nothing to analyse with.", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        if args.path:
            print(f"Queued {store.mark_pending(args.path)} versions.", file=sys.stderr)
        n = analyze_pending(store, analyst, notify, settings.notify_min_severity, args.limit)
        print(f"Analysed {n} versions.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "watch":
        watch(
            store,
            PortalClient(settings.portal_url, settings.portal_token),
            _analyst(settings, store),
            notify,
            args.interval or settings.interval_seconds,
            settings.notify_min_severity,
            args.analyze_baseline,
        )
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "findings":
        items = store.findings(None if args.all else "open")
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(items, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
            return 0
        for f in items:
            print(f"#{f['id']} [{f['severity']}] {f['title']}  ({f['status']}, from {f['path']})")
            print(f"    {f['detail']}")
            if f["suggested_action"]:
                print(f"    Action: {f['suggested_action']}")
        if not items:
            print("No findings.")
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "status":
        q = store.db.execute
        print(f"current files:   {len(store.current())}")
        print(f"versions stored: {q('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM versions').fetchone()[0]}")
        for row in q("SELECT analysis_status, COUNT(*) n FROM versions GROUP BY 1").fetchall():
            print(f"  {row[0]:8} {row[1]}")
        print(f"polls:           {q('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM polls').fetchone()[0]}")
        print(f"open findings:   {len(store.findings('open'))}")
        return 0
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def load_dotenv(path: Path = Path(".env")) -> None:
    """Load KEY=VALUE lines into os.environ without overriding variables that are already set."""
    if not path.exists():

    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():

        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:

"""Client for the customer portal API: list files with checksums, download one file."""

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import quote

import httpx


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RemoteFile:
    path: str
    sha256: str
    size: int | None


class PortalError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class PortalClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, token: str, http: httpx.Client | None = None):
        if not base_url or not token:
            raise PortalError(
                "SOONY_PORTAL_URL and SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN must be set (see .env.example)"
            )
        self._base = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._http = http or httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=15.0))
        self._headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    def _get(self, url: str, attempts: int = 4) -> httpx.Response:
        """GET with retries on dropped connections and server errors."""
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            try:
                resp = self._http.get(url, headers=self._headers)
                if resp.status_code < 500 or attempt == attempts - 1:
                    return resp
            except httpx.TransportError:
                if attempt == attempts - 1:
                    raise
            time.sleep(2**attempt)
        raise PortalError(f"GET {url} failed")

    def list_files(self) -> list[RemoteFile]:
        resp = self._get(f"{self._base}/api/v1/files")
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise PortalError(f"listing failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:200]}")
        body = resp.json()
        items = body.get("files", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
        files = []
        for item in items:
            size = item.get("bytes", item.get("size"))
            files.append(RemoteFile(path=item["path"], sha256=item["sha256"], size=size))
        return files

    def download(self, path: str) -> bytes:
        url = f"{self._base}/api/v1/files/{quote(path, safe='/')}"
        resp = self._get(url)
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise PortalError(f"download of {path} failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}")
        return resp.content

    def download_archive(self) -> bytes:
        resp = self._get(f"{self._base}/api/v1/archive.zip")
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise PortalError(f"archive download failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}")
        return resp.content
"""
Provider-neutral agent loop interface.

The agent only knows about text, images and tools. Each backend translates that into its own
API: llm/anthropic_backend.py (Anthropic SDK) and llm/openai_backend.py (OpenAI SDK, also for
OpenAI-compatible servers such as llama.cpp).
"""

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Protocol

from ask_soony.extract import Image


@dataclass
class Tool:
    name: str
    description: str
    schema: dict


@dataclass
class RunResult:
    final_text: str
    tool_calls: int
    stop_reason: str
    usage: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


# Runs one tool call and returns the text result. Raising ToolError marks the result as an error.
ToolHandler = Callable[[str, dict], str]


class ToolError(Exception):
    pass


class Backend(Protocol):
    provider: str
    model: str

    def run(
        self,
        system: str,
        text: str,
        images: list[Image],
        tools: list[Tool],
        handler: ToolHandler,
        should_stop: Callable[[], bool],
        max_turns: int = 12,
    ) -> RunResult: ...


def make_backend(provider: str, model: str, api_key: str, base_url: str, effort: str) -> Backend:
    if provider == "anthropic":
        from ask_soony.llm.anthropic_backend import AnthropicBackend

        return AnthropicBackend(model=model, api_key=REDACTED, base_url=base_url, effort=effort)
    if provider in {"openai", "llamacpp", "openai-compatible"}:
        from ask_soony.llm.openai_backend import OpenAIBackend

        return OpenAIBackend(model=model, api_key=REDACTED, base_url=base_url, provider=provider)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown ASK_LLM_PROVIDER {provider!r}: use anthropic, openai or llamacpp")
"""Claude backend: manual tool loop on the Messages API via the official Anthropic SDK."""

import base64
from collections.abc import Callable

import anthropic

from ask_soony.extract import Image
from ask_soony.llm import RunResult, Tool, ToolError, ToolHandler

# Server-side refusal fallback: on a policy decline the API re-runs the request on a fallback
# model inside the same call.
FALLBACK_BETA = "server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"
FALLBACK_MODELS = {
    "claude-opus-5-5",
    "claude-opus-5",
    "claude-sonnet-5-5",
    "claude-fable-5-1",
    "claude-fable-5-2",
}


class AnthropicBackend:
    provider = "anthropic"

    def __init__(self, model: str, api_key: str = "", base_url: str = "", effort: str = "medium"):
        kwargs = {}
        if api_key:
            kwargs["api_key"] = api_key
        if base_url:
            kwargs["base_url"] = base_url
        # Without an explicit key the SDK resolves ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an `ant auth login` profile.
        self.client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=4, **kwargs)
        self.model = model
        self.effort = effort

    def run(
        self,
        system: str,
        text: str,
        images: list[Image],
        tools: list[Tool],
        handler: ToolHandler,
        should_stop: Callable[[], bool],
        max_turns: int = 12,
    ) -> RunResult:
        content: list[dict] = [
            {
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "base64",
                    "media_type": img.media_type,
                    "data": base64.standard_b64encode(img.data).decode("ascii"),
                },
            }
            for img in images
        ]
        content.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": content}]
        tool_defs = [
            {"name": t.name, "description": t.description, "input_schema": t.schema} for t in tools
        ]
        calls = 0
        usage = {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}
        stop = "max_turns"
        final_text = ""
        for _ in range(max_turns):
            params = dict(
                model=self.model,
                max_tokens=16000,
                system=[{"type": "text", "text": system, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
                tools=tool_defs,
                messages=messages,
                output_config={"effort": self.effort},
            )
            if self.model in FALLBACK_MODELS:
                response = self.client.beta.messages.create(
                    **params, betas=[FALLBACK_BETA], fallbacks="default"
                )
            else:
                response = self.client.messages.create(**params)
            usage["input_tokens"] += response.usage.input_tokens
            usage["output_tokens"] += response.usage.output_tokens
            stop = response.stop_reason or "unknown"
            final_text = "\n".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text")
            if stop == "refusal":
                break
            # Keep the whole assistant turn (thinking and tool_use blocks) unchanged.
            messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
            if stop == "pause_turn":
                continue
            tool_uses = [b for b in response.content if b.type == "tool_use"]
            if stop != "tool_use" or not tool_uses:
                break
            results = []
            for block in tool_uses:
                calls += 1
                try:
                    out = handler(block.name, dict(block.input))
                    results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": block.id, "content": out})
                except ToolError as e:
                    results.append(
                        {
                            "type": "tool_result",
                            "tool_use_id": block.id,
                            "content": str(e),
                            "is_error": True,
                        }
                    )
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
            if should_stop():
                stop = "submitted"
                break
        return RunResult(final_text=final_text, tool_calls=calls, stop_reason=stop, usage=usage)

OpenAI-compatible backend: OpenAI itself, or a local llama.cpp server (`llama-server --jinja`,
which speaks the same chat completions API with tool calls) via ASK_LLM_BASE_URL.
"""

import base64
import json
from collections.abc import Callable

from openai import OpenAI

from ask_soony.extract import Image
from ask_soony.llm import RunResult, Tool, ToolError, ToolHandler


class OpenAIBackend:
    def __init__(self, model: str, api_key: str = "", base_url: str = "", provider: str = "openai"):
        kwargs = {}
        if base_url:
            kwargs["base_url"] = base_url
        # Local servers ignore the key, but the SDK requires one.
        if api_key or base_url:
            kwargs["api_key"] = api_key or "local"
        self.client = OpenAI(max_retries=4, **kwargs)
        self.model = model
        self.provider = provider

    def run(
        self,
        system: str,
        text: str,
        images: list[Image],
        tools: list[Tool],
        handler: ToolHandler,
        should_stop: Callable[[], bool],
        max_turns: int = 12,
    ) -> RunResult:
        content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
        for img in images:
            b64 = base64.standard_b64encode(img.data).decode("ascii")
            content.append(
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:{img.media_type};base64,{b64}"}}
            )
        messages: list[dict] = [
            {"role": "system", "content": system},
            {"role": "user", "content": content},
        ]
        tool_defs = [
            {
                "type": "function",
                "function": {"name": t.name, "description": t.description, "parameters": t.schema},
            }
            for t in tools
        ]
        calls = 0
        usage = {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}
        stop = "max_turns"
        final_text = ""
        for _ in range(max_turns):
            response = self.client.chat.completions.create(
                model=self.model, messages=messages, tools=tool_defs
            )
            if response.usage:
                usage["input_tokens"] += response.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
                usage["output_tokens"] += response.usage.completion_tokens or 0
            choice = response.choices[0]
            msg = choice.message
            stop = choice.finish_reason or "unknown"
            final_text = msg.content or ""
            messages.append(msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
            if not msg.tool_calls:
                break
            for call in msg.tool_calls:
                calls += 1
                try:
                    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
                    out = handler(call.function.name, args)
                except (ToolError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
                    out = f"Error: {e}"
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": out})
            if should_stop():
                stop = "submitted"
                break
        return RunResult(final_text=final_text, tool_calls=calls, stop_reason=stop, usage=usage)
"""Command line: ask-soony download | poll | analyze | watch | findings | status."""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from ask_soony.agent import Analyst
from ask_soony.config import Settings
from ask_soony.llm import make_backend
from ask_soony.notify import build_notifiers
from ask_soony.portal import PortalClient
from ask_soony.store import Store
from ask_soony.watcher import analyze_pending, describe_poll, mirror, poll, watch


def _analyst(settings: Settings, store: Store) -> Analyst | None:
    if settings.llm_provider == "none":
        return None
    backend = make_backend(
        settings.llm_provider,
        settings.llm_model,
        settings.llm_api_key,
        settings.llm_base_url,
        settings.llm_effort,
    )
    return Analyst(store, backend)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ask-soony", description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    p_dl = sub.add_parser(
        "download", help="One-off: fetch the portal and write all files under their paths"
    )
    p_dl.add_argument("dest", nargs="?", default="data/portal", help="Target folder")
    p_poll = sub.add_parser("poll", help="Poll once: store new versions, report changes")
    p_poll.add_argument(
        "--analyze-baseline", action="store_true", help="Queue the first snapshot for analysis too"
    )
    p_an = sub.add_parser("analyze", help="Analyse pending versions")
    p_an.add_argument("--limit", type=int)
    p_an.add_argument("--path", help="Queue current files under this path prefix first")
    p_watch = sub.add_parser("watch", help="Poll, analyse and notify in a loop")
    p_watch.add_argument(
        "--interval", type=int, help="Seconds between polls (default ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS)"
    )
    p_watch.add_argument("--analyze-baseline", action="store_true")
    p_f = sub.add_parser("findings", help="Print findings")
    p_f.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="Include resolved findings")
    p_f.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    sub.add_parser("status", help="Versions, pending analyses and open findings")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    settings = Settings.from_env()
    store = Store(settings.data_dir)
    notify = build_notifiers(settings.notifiers, settings.discord_webhook_url, settings.webhook_url)

    if args.cmd == "download":
        result = poll(store, PortalClient(settings.portal_url, settings.portal_token))
        n = mirror(store, Path(args.dest))
        changes = describe_poll(result)
        print(f"{n} files in {args.dest}" + (f" ({changes.title})" if changes else ""))
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "poll":
        result = poll(
            store, PortalClient(settings.portal_url, settings.portal_token), args.analyze_baseline
        )
        event = describe_poll(result)
        if event:
            notify.send(event)
        else:
            print("No changes.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "analyze":
        analyst = _analyst(settings, store)
        if analyst is None:
            print("ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none: nothing to analyse with.", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        if args.path:
            print(f"Queued {store.mark_pending(args.path)} versions.", file=sys.stderr)
        n = analyze_pending(store, analyst, notify, settings.notify_min_severity, args.limit)
        print(f"Analysed {n} versions.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "watch":
        watch(
            store,
            PortalClient(settings.portal_url, settings.portal_token),
            _analyst(settings, store),
            notify,
            args.interval or settings.interval_seconds,
            settings.notify_min_severity,
            args.analyze_baseline,
        )
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "findings":
        items = store.findings(None if args.all else "open")
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(items, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
            return 0
        for f in items:
            print(f"#{f['id']} [{f['severity']}] {f['title']}  ({f['status']}, from {f['path']})")
            print(f"    {f['detail']}")
            if f["suggested_action"]:
                print(f"    Action: {f['suggested_action']}")
        if not items:
            print("No findings.")
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "status":
        q = store.db.execute
        print(f"current files:   {len(store.current())}")
        print(f"versions stored: {q('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM versions').fetchone()[0]}")
        for row in q("SELECT analysis_status, COUNT(*) n FROM versions GROUP BY 1").fetchall():
            print(f"  {row[0]:8} {row[1]}")
        print(f"polls:           {q('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM polls').fetchone()[0]}")
        print(f"open findings:   {len(store.findings('open'))}")
        return 0
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.text:
I built the event impact agent. It reads news items and supplier notices and works out which supplier, part and product each one affects, and how. I ran it live on the portal's current news feed, and the tests pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**What I added**
- **`src/ask_soony/impact.py`** (~250 lines), the agent itself:
  - **Finding events:** it treats any portal file inside a `news/`, `notices/`, `events/` or `alerts/` folder as an event. A JSON news feed is split into one event per item. You can also pass in plain text, like a weather or strike report.
  - **What it reads:** before each run it reads the small data files in `master/`, `erp/` and `logistics/`, plus each supplier's profile and parts list. No supplier or part names are in the code, so new files are picked up without changes.
  - **How it answers:** one LLM call traces the event from region or route to supplier, then to the part (including parts built into other parts), then to the product through the bill of materials. It returns a fixed structure: for each affected link, the effect (delay, shortage, quality and so on), how it happens, from when, whether it risks the launch, how severe it is, and the evidence. It also gives an overall launch risk, a recommendation and any contradictions between sources.
  - **Check against made-up IDs:** any supplier, part or product ID the model names that doesn't appear in the data is listed in `unknown_ids` and printed as a warning.
  - **Where results go:** `data/state/impacts.json`, one entry per event. That's where `plan.md` says shared state lives, so the UI and Jonas's criticality agent can read it. Events already analysed are skipped unless you pass `--force`.
- **CLI:** `ask-soony impact`, with these options:
  - `--path soony/news` to only look at events under a path
  - `--text "Port strike in Yantian…"` to analyse a free-text event
  - `--force` to re-analyse events already done
  - `--list` to print stored results without calling the model
- **`config.py`:** it now accepts the names your `.env` uses (`URL` without `https://`, `TOKEN`), and switches to OpenAI when only `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set.
- **`tests/test_impact.py`:** offline tests for spotting event files, splitting news feeds and flagging unknown IDs.

**Live result on the current data:** both magnet export-ban news items came back as **no launch risk**, which is the false-alarm answer `plan.md` expects for that drop (finding #7). The agent traced the magnets correctly: they sit inside PackRight's collector's box and go only into the Collector's Edition, and the effect starts in December.

**What could go wrong**
- The data context is about 62k characters and is sent in full on every call. That's fine at this size, but it will need trimming if the portal grows a lot.
- PDFs are read as text only, so a scanned notice with no text layer would come through empty.
- I haven't yet run it on the supplier notices (Nowak's planned stop and rush offer, PackRight's licence notice). To do that: `uv run ask-soony impact --path suppliers`.

I also haven't added your line to `PROGRESS.md`. Do you want me to do that and commit this as one commit?

# Verifier

Every number in Soony's systems is a claim. The verifier checks each claim against the documents that confirm or contradict it, decides which to believe, and says who to ask when the data can't settle it.

This folder holds the notes and the verifier scripts.

## Pipeline

1. **Link:** connect all records that describe the same order, delivery or lot
2. **Read:** turn each document into claims
3. **Judge:** where claims disagree, decide which to believe
4. **Route:** when the data can't settle it, decide who to ask

## 1. Linking

Before anything can be compared, we need to know which records belong together. This is about half the work.

### The chain of one order

```
PO line → confirmation → shipping document → shipment → delivery note → goods receipt → stock batch → inspection
```

| Record | What it is | Who owns it |
|---|---|---|
| PO (purchase order) | Soony's order: part, quantity, price, date | Soony buyer, in SAP |
| Confirmation | The supplier's reply to a PO: what it promises to deliver, when, at what price | Supplier |
| Shipping document | What the supplier physically sent (shipping advice, packing list) | Supplier |
| Shipment | Soony's record of the transport: container, flight or truck, with ETA and status | Soony logistics (ERP feed; Excel tracker kept by hand) |
| Delivery note | Paper that travels with the goods; Hamburg may correct it by hand | Supplier writes it; Hamburg annotates it |
| Goods receipt | Hamburg's booking of what arrived, typed in by hand | Soony Hamburg, in SAP |
| Stock batch | What SAP believes is in the warehouse, created by the receipt | Soony, in SAP |
| Inspection report | Quality check of a received lot | Soony Hamburg quality |

### Keys between records

| Link | Owners | Key | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|---|
| PO ↔ confirmation | Soony ↔ supplier | PO number | `po_number` in SAP; filename `OA<conf>_<PO>.pdf` |
| PO ↔ shipping document | Soony ↔ supplier | PO number | filename `Shipping_advice_<AWB>_<PO>.pdf`, `PL_<ref>_<PO>.pdf` |
| PO ↔ shipment | Soony ↔ Soony | PO number (no line) | `open_shipments.csv` `po_numbers`, several joined with `\|` |
| Shipment ↔ shipping document | Soony ↔ supplier | Air waybill / container number | `open_shipments.csv` `reference`; inside the document |
| Shipment ↔ tracker | Soony ERP ↔ Soony Excel | Shipment id | `shipment_id`; the tracker uses supplier names |
| PO line ↔ goods receipt | Soony ↔ Soony Hamburg | PO number + line | `goods_receipts.csv` `po_number`, `po_line` |
| Goods receipt ↔ delivery note scan | Soony Hamburg ↔ supplier (+ Hamburg's handwriting) | Delivery note number | `goods_receipts.csv` `delivery_note`; filename `<date>_<WZ\|SN\|DN>-….jpg/png` |
| Goods receipt ↔ stock | Soony ↔ Soony | Batch = receipt number | `gr_number` = `stock_snapshot.csv` `batch` |
| Batch ↔ inspection | Soony ↔ Soony Hamburg quality | Batch number | filename `inspection_report_<batch>.pdf` |
| Anything ↔ part | Soony master ↔ supplier numbering | Material id | `CMP-…`; PackRight documents use `PR-…` (contract Annex C) |
| Anything ↔ supplier | Soony (several formats) | Supplier id | `SUP-0019`; legacy PO file uses `19`; tracker uses names |

### Normalise before linking

- **Legacy PO export:** SAP field names (`EBELN` = PO, `EBELP` = line, `LIFNR` = supplier, `MATNR` = material), `;` separator, decimal commas, `MM/DD/YYYY` dates. Line `00010` is line 1 and `00510` is line 51 (confirmed: all legacy receipts link).
- **Supplier:** numeric id, `SUP-` id, folder name and display name all map to one id.
- **Part:** supplier part numbers map to `CMP-` ids.
- **Cancellations:** negative quantities.

### Unlinked records are findings

A record that links to nothing is reported, not dropped. Examples: a receipt with no PO (the pre-order pins), a PO line with no confirmation, a scan with no receipt, a shipment line with no confirmation.

Links have a confidence level: an **exact key** match is certain. A **fuzzy** match (same supplier, part, date range and quantity) needs review.

## 2. What can disagree

Five things:

1. **Quantity:** how many were ordered, shipped, received or are in stock
2. **Date:** when something ships or arrives
3. **Status:** usable or blocked, approved or conditional, in transit or arrived
4. **Revision:** which version of a part (e.g. sleeve artwork rev. B vs. rev. C)
5. **Price:** what Soony pays vs. what the contract allows

## 3. Who would know: evidence by fact

| Fact | Who would know | Example |
|---|---|---|
| What was ordered | SAP purchase order | PO for 8,000 art books |
| What was shipped | The supplier's own shipping document | Shipping advice: 28,000 of 48,000 flew |
| What arrived and in what condition | Physical evidence at Hamburg (delivery note, inspection report) | Handwritten 8,000; 9 of 125 statues failed |
| Price and terms | The contract | Boise ships EXW; prices fixed for the year |
| Anything else | Spreadsheets (lowest weight) | The shipment tracker |

### When they disagree

Start with the source that would know, then apply three checks:

- **Newer beats older** for the same event. The shipping advice from 21 Nov beats the shipment feed.
- **A second independent source settles it.** The PO says 8,000, which backs the handwritten 8,000 against SAP's 80,000.
- **Typical error patterns raise suspicion:** a factor of 10, swapped digits, wrong units.

| Outcome | Meaning | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Resolved** | The evidence agrees | Propose the fix |
| **Likely** | Strong evidence, but not conclusive | A person confirms |
| **Can't tell** | The data can't settle it | Ask whoever would know |

## 4. Who to ask

| Question | Ask | Example |
|---|---|---|
| What arrived? | **Hamburg** (count or check it) | Is it 8,000 or 80,000 art books? |
| What shipped? | **The supplier** | What is on the plane? |
| What is allowed? | **An approver** from policy PP-07 (vacant role → Head of Procurement) | May the failed statue lot be used? |
| Which version is valid? | **Marketing** | Sleeve rev. B or rev. C? |

Contact suppliers only about contradictions that matter. They stop replying when spammed.

## Linker: status and usage

Code in `linker/`. M1 and M2 are done:
- **Linked:** spreadsheets, master data, supplier profiles, and documents by their filename keys.
- **Issue priority:** every issue is marked `live` or `closed` and has a `due` date. Live issues come first, soonest first.
- **M3, done:** the documents' contents, from the image recognizer's readings (`--readings`, default `data/store/image_recognizer`). Delivery notes vs receipts, shipping documents vs PO lines, failed inspections vs stock, and filename vs content keys.
- **Next:** an adapter for `stock_update_*.xlsx` (new drop, still `unknown`).

Status: [linker/linker_strategy.md](linker/linker_strategy.md).

# Dashboard contract

How modules plug into the decision inbox (`scripts/dashboard.sh`). Everything is JSON files; modules never call the API.

## 1. Drop a card file

Write `data/store/<module>_cards.json` (any name matching `*cards*.json`). The API reads all of them on every request, so new files show up within 5 s. Cards merge by `id` (later file name wins, duplicates are logged); each card is tagged with `source_file` and `module` (the file stem). `editions`, `parts`, `now`, `hours_left`, `packing_ends` come from the first file that has them (alphabetically; the verifier's `decision_cards.json`).

`ASK_SOONY_STATE` overrides the folder scan: one path, a glob, or a comma-separated list.

```json
{
  "editions": [], "parts": [],
  "cards": [{
    "id": "stable-unique-id", "title": "...", "edition": "...", "part": "...",
    "at_risk": 0, "at_risk_if_acted": 0, "act_by": "ISO time", "runs_dry": "ISO time|null",
    "stage": "before_arrival | after_dock",
    "system_says": "...", "paper_says": "...",
    "evidence": ["text" | {"doc_path": "", "page": 1, "quote": "", "language": "", "translation": ""}],
    "options": ["text" | {"action": "", "cost": "", "effect": "", "recommended": true}],
    "messages": [{"to_role": "", "to_email": "", "subject": "", "body": ""}],
    "decision": null, "blocked_only": false
  }]
}
```

Keep card ids stable between runs, otherwise a human decision no longer matches its card.

## 2. Read decisions before acting (sender)

`data/state/decisions.json`, keyed by card id, written when a human clicks:

```json
{ "<card_id>": { "action": "allow_once | allow_always | edit | dismiss", "note": null, "ts": "ISO" } }
```

- `allow_once`: send this card's `messages` once. `allow_always`: send, and send future cards of the same kind without asking.
- `edit`: `note` holds the human's changes; do not send until the card is re-issued.
- `dismiss`: never send.
- `data/state/mode.json`: `{"mode": "ask" | "autonomous"}`. In `ask` send nothing without a decision for the card; in `autonomous` send without waiting.

## 3. Write message status back

`data/state/actions.json`, either `{ "<card_id>": {...} }` or a list of records:

```json
{ "card_id": "...", "status": "sent | replied", "at": "ISO", "reply": "optional text" }
```

The API merges the record into the card as `action_status`; the UI shows a SENT or REPLIED badge.

## 4. Activity feed

`/api/feed` merges, newest first, events `{at, actor, text, ref?}` from:

- `data/state/feed.json` (UI clicks; modules may append the same shape),
- the watcher store `data/store/ask-soony.db` (polls with changes, new or changed file versions with their summary when the `changes` table exists, analyses, findings), read-only,
- the mail log: `data/outbox/*.json` (sent) and `data/inbox/*.eml` (received).

Missing files, tables or columns are skipped silently. `ASK_DATA_DIR` moves the store folder.

- **discover.py:** classifies files by their columns (CSV, XLSX, JSON) or filename pattern (documents). Unmatched files are reported as `unknown`.
- **normalize.py:** cleans up supplier ids, PO lines, lists, numbers and dates.
- **adapters/:** turn each file kind into records.
- **rules.py:** link rules (exact joins plus "must have a partner") and structural checks.
- **graph.py:** build, save, trace.

**Unchanged design choices:** everything is rebuilt on each run, pandas does the work in memory, and SQLite only stores the result.

## Price it and act: `impact/` and `act/`

```bash
uv run python -m verifier.impact   # parts: needed, book stock, usable, gap; copies at risk per edition
uv run python -m verifier.act      # decision cards → data/store/decision_cards.html (+ .json)
```

- **impact/shortfall.py** works out copies at risk:
  - **Demand still to pack:** day-one demand (`products.csv`) minus packed copies (the newest `stock_update`), times the parts per copy (`bom.csv`).
  - **Usable stock:** the newest book stock minus live linker issues with a stock effect: booked but not delivered, failed inspection, wrong part booked, old revision.
  - **Not counted:** parts a supplier says it fits into another part, such as the magnets.
  - **Ways to close a gap:** inbound waiting at the port, supplier offers, and arrivals after launch (shown, but they don't help).
- **impact/timing.py** works out when each part runs out:
  - **Packing windows** come from the launch plan's `Shifts` sheet. **Now** is the time of the newest stock figures, not the machine clock.
  - **Run-out time** = usable stock ÷ (packing rate × parts per copy), walked through the shifts.
  - **Act-by time** = run-out time minus the lead time. The lead time is read from the document, e.g. "loaded within 4 h" plus "about 9 hours driving" gives 13 h.
- **Each edition shows two numbers:** copies at risk **now**, and **if you act in time** (collect, order, concede).
- **act/cards.py** makes one decision card per cause, with copies at risk, *system says* vs *paper says*, the options, the decision needed, and ready emails routed by the table above. Supplier addresses come from the profiles. Nothing is sent automatically: a person clicks *Email* (mailto) or *Copy text*. **For an email agent:** `data/store/decision_cards.json` lists every card with its messages (`to_email`, `subject`, `body`) and `act_by`. The sender address must be registered in the portal.

## Building blocks

- **Claim store:** one shared table of claims, recording what, value, source, issuer and time. Every step reads from it and writes to it.
- **Linker:** builds the chain above, exact keys first, fuzzy matches flagged.
- **Reader:** turns each new or changed file into claims. Text PDFs go through text extraction. Scans and images go to a multimodal model (no training). Printed and handwritten values are kept separate.
- **Judge:** applies the evidence rules.
- **Router:** picks who to ask and drafts the question.

Yes, this can work, and the pieces mostly fit already. I changed nothing; this is from reading the branches. One problem has to be fixed before any merge, though.

**Blocker: the `verifier` branch contains confidential portal data.** Commit `b563d6a` ("Track portal data to see changes") force-added about 330 portal files under `data/portal/`: contracts, scans, purchase orders and supplier documents. `data/` is gitignored on `main`, and the rules say never to commit portal data. Those files are already on GitHub in that branch's history. Before merging, Farhan should remove them from the branch history, not just delete them in a new commit. That branch also removes the `soony-data/` line from `.gitignore` and adds `.claude/` to it. Ignoring `.claude/` would drop the team's committed hooks from new commits.

**How the three systems would line up**

| System | Job | Where it lives now | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Data verification | Three-way match and linking: PO ↔ confirmation ↔ shipment ↔ delivery note ↔ goods receipt ↔ stock ↔ inspection. Also reads the scans and works out shortfall and timing | `verifier/` (`linker/`, `image_recognizer/`, `impact/`) | Issues in `data/store/verifier.db`, copies at risk |
| 2. Event verification | News or notice → supplier → part → product, with a launch-risk verdict | `src/ask_soony/impact.py` (my branch, `feat/predictor`) | `data/state/impacts.json` |
| 3. Act | Turns findings into decision cards and emails; a human clicks; message status is written back | `verifier/act/` (cards) and `akshat/dashboard` (inbox UI and contract) | `*cards*.json`, then `decisions.json`, then `actions.json` |

**Why it fits**
- Akshat's `docs/dashboard_contract.md` is already the bridge between them. Modules talk only through JSON files: each drops a `data/store/<module>_cards.json`, and the dashboard merges them. The verifier's `act/` already writes `decision_cards.json` in that format.
- Plugging in event verification is small: one function that turns each `impacts.json` entry into a card and writes `data/store/events_cards.json`. A false alarm like the magnet news becomes a "no launch risk" card, or none at all.
- No module needs to import another, so each team member keeps their own folder.

**Things to settle when integrating**
1. **Two code roots.** `verifier/` sits at the repo top level, and the rest is under `src/ask_soony/`; making `verifier/` importable needed a `pythonpath = ["."]` setting. For readability, move everything under one package, for example `src/ask_soony/verify/` (data checks), `src/ask_soony/events/` (my agent) and `src/ask_soony/act/` (cards).
2. **Two modules named `impact`.** `verifier/impact` is shortfall and timing maths; mine traces events. Rename mine to `events`.
3. **Overlapping state files.** There are three shapes: `plan.md`'s `Finding/Impact/Decision` schema, the verifier's issues table, and the dashboard's card format. Treat the card as the one shape every system hands to "Act", and keep each system's internal format private.
4. **Event verdicts don't use the verifier's numbers yet.** My agent reads raw stock. It would be more accurate if it read the verifier's "usable stock" and run-out times, for example to confirm that boxes in stock cover the Collector's Edition. That's an optional second step.
5. **Dependencies.** The verifier adds `pandas`, `tqdm` and `claude-agent-sdk`. That's fine, but expect a conflict in `uv.lock` when merging.
6. **Sending emails.** `verifier/act` only makes mailto links, while the contract expects a sender that reads `decisions.json`. Jonas's watcher-dashboard branch is the natural home for that sender, but it hasn't been written yet.

Suggested order:
1. Farhan removes the data commit from `verifier`.
2. Merge `verifier` and `akshat/dashboard`.
3. Rebase `feat/predictor`, rename my module to `events`, and add the card writer.
4. Add the sender.

I can do step 3 when you're ready.

Yes, in three places:

1. **`AGENTS.md`**, under "The rules that shape the code": *"Confidential. Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API."*
2. **`.gitignore` on `main`**, lines 6–7: `# Portal data: fetch it through the API, never commit it` followed by `data/`.
3. **`docs/challenge.md`**, which holds Lio's own rules: *"Use the challenge data only for this hackathon and do not share it outside the team."* The first part of this rule appears both at the top and in section 12.

The repo is private, so committing the files there isn't the same as sharing them outside the team. But it breaks the team's explicit rule. It also puts confidential customer data permanently in the git history, where anyone given access to the repo later can see it.

Because `data/` is gitignored, those files can only get committed on purpose, with `git add -f` or by changing the ignore rules. The commit message, "Track portal data to see changes", suggests Farhan did it deliberately to see how files change between drops. Jonas's watcher already does that: it keeps every file version in the local store.

# Plan: organise the repo into verification / predictor / dispatcher

## Context
Code is spread over three roots: `src/ask_soony/` (watcher, store, LLM backends, CLI),
top-level `verifier/` (Farhan: linker, image_recognizer, impact maths, act/cards) and
`feat/predictor` (my `src/ask_soony/impact.py`, event tracing). Two modules are called
`impact`, "act" lives inside the verifier, and `verifier/` only imports via a
`pythonpath = ["."]` hack. Goal: one package, three clearly named systems that talk only
through JSON files (Akshat's `docs/dashboard_contract.md`), readable by any teammate.

## Target layout
```
src/ask_soony/
  core/            shared plumbing (moved, unchanged)
    config.py portal.py store.py extract.py watcher.py notify.py llm/
  verification/    "are the numbers true?"  (from verifier/)
    linker/        three-way match: PO ↔ confirmation ↔ shipment ↔ DN ↔ GR ↔ stock ↔ inspection
    reader/        = image_recognizer (scans → claims)
    shortfall.py   = verifier/impact/shortfall.py
    timing.py      = verifier/impact/timing.py
    README.md      = verifier/README.md
  predictor/       "what will happen?"  (events + arrival forecast)
    events.py      = my impact.py (news/notice → supplier → part → product)
    cards.py       NEW: impacts.json → data/store/predictor_cards.json
  dispatcher/      "what do we do, and do it"
    cards.py render.py   = verifier/act/*
    sender.py      NEW later (Jonas): read decisions.json, send, write actions.json
  api.py feed.py   dashboard backend (Akshat, unchanged)
  cli.py           one entry: ask-soony verify | predict | dispatch | watch | ...
tests/verification/ tests/predictor/ tests/dispatcher/   (moved from verifier/**/tests)
docs/architecture.md   one diagram + the JSON contracts between the three systems
```
Data flow (files only, no cross-imports except dispatcher reading verification results):
`watcher → store` → `verification` (issues, shortfall) + `predictor` (impacts)
→ `*cards*.json` → dashboard → `decisions.json` → `dispatcher` → `actions.json`.

## Steps
0. **Prerequisite (Farhan):** rewrite `verifier` branch history to drop commit `b563d6a`
   (`data/portal/` committed); restore `data/` + `.claude/` lines in `.gitignore`.
1. Merge order: `verifier` → `akshat/dashboard` → `jonas/watcher-dashboard` → `feat/predictor`
   into a new branch `refactor/layout` (each owner agrees; announce in PROGRESS.md Now line).
2. `git mv` files into the layout above (keeps history). Pure moves in one commit.
3. Rewrite imports in a second commit: `verifier.linker` → `ask_soony.verification.linker`,
   `verifier.image_recognizer` → `ask_soony.verification.reader`,
   `verifier.impact` → `ask_soony.verification`, `verifier.act` → `ask_soony.dispatcher`,
   `ask_soony.<core mod>` → `ask_soony.core.<mod>` (~35 files, mechanical sed + ruff `--fix` for import order).
4. `pyproject.toml`: drop `pythonpath=["."]` and `verifier` testpath; testpaths = `["tests"]`;
   move per-file ruff ignores to new paths.
5. CLI: add subcommands wrapping the existing `__main__` entry points
   (`verify build|trace|issues`, `verify read`, `predict [--text]`, `dispatch`), keep
   `python -m ask_soony.verification.linker` working.
6. New small code: `predictor/cards.py` maps each impact with `launch_risk != "no"` to the
   dashboard card shape (stable id = event id); false alarms become one info card.
7. Write `docs/architecture.md`; update README, `plan.md` §4 module names.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest` (all moved tests pass, same count as before the move)
- `uv run ruff check src tests`
- `uv run ask-soony verify build` prints the same issue counts as `python -m verifier.linker build` did
- `uv run ask-soony predict --path soony/news` → magnet news "NO launch risk"
- `uv run ask-soony dispatch` writes `decision_cards.json`; `scripts/dashboard.sh` shows
  verifier + predictor cards together
- `git ls-files data/` is empty

# Plan: integrate `verifier` with `feat/predictor` + `main` for testing

## Context
Farhan's `verifier` (PR #2, 38 commits) is not in `main` yet. We want to run it together
with the event impact agent (`feat/predictor`) and latest `main` now, while keeping the
eventual merge to `main` easy. Catch: `verifier` commit `b563d6a` committed ~330
confidential portal files under `data/portal/` and dropped the `data/` rule from
`.gitignore`. Our integration must not carry that data into our history.

Read-only check (`git merge-tree`): main ↔ feat/predictor and feat/predictor ↔ verifier
merge with **no conflicts**.

## Approach: one integration branch, verifier squashed without the data
1. `git switch feat/predictor && git merge origin/main` (picks up "Add interview gaps to plan").
2. `git switch -c integration/verifier` from that.
3. `git merge --squash origin/verifier` → staged, not committed.
4. Drop the data from the squash: `git rm -r --cached -q data/` (files stay on disk, ignored).
5. Fix `.gitignore`: keep `data/` and the `soony-data/` lines; do **not** take the
   `.claude/` ignore line (it would hide the team's committed hooks). Keep the rest.
6. Commit: "Integrate verifier (PR #2) without portal data", body notes source commit
   `origin/verifier@43a8e69` and that data was excluded.
7. `uv sync` (verifier adds pandas, tqdm, claude-agent-sdk).
8. Check `git ls-files data/` is empty before any push. Push `integration/verifier` only
   after the Entire checks (`entire status`, `entire brain status`).

Why squash: a normal merge would pull `b563d6a` (the data) into our history and later
into `main`. The squash gives one clean commit with identical code. When Farhan merges a
cleaned `verifier` into `main`, our branch rebases on it with no or trivial conflicts
(same file contents); our squash commit then becomes empty and drops out.

## Later merge to main
- Farhan rewrites `verifier` without `b563d6a` (or squash-merges PR #2 excluding `data/`).
- Then: `git rebase origin/main` on `feat/predictor`, open PR for `feat/predictor` only.
- `integration/verifier` is a throwaway test branch; delete after.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest` (tests/ + verifier/ via the verifier's pytest config) and `uv run ruff check`
- `uv run python -m verifier.linker build` → summary of links and issues
- `uv run python -m verifier.impact` and `uv run python -m verifier.act` → `data/store/decision_cards.json`
- `uv run ask-soony impact --path soony/news` still gives "NO launch risk"
- `git ls-files data/ | wc -l` → 0

# Plan: organise the repo into verification / predictor / dispatcher

## Context
Code is spread over three roots: `src/ask_soony/` (watcher, store, LLM backends, CLI),
top-level `verifier/` (Farhan: linker, image_recognizer, impact maths, act/cards) and
`feat/predictor` (my `src/ask_soony/impact.py`, event tracing). Two modules are called
`impact`, "act" lives inside the verifier, and `verifier/` only imports via a
`pythonpath = ["."]` hack. Goal: one package, three clearly named systems that talk only
through JSON files (Akshat's `docs/dashboard_contract.md`), readable by any teammate.

## Target layout
```
src/ask_soony/
  core/            shared plumbing (moved, unchanged)
    config.py portal.py store.py extract.py watcher.py notify.py llm/
  verification/    "are the numbers true?"  (from verifier/)
    linker/        three-way match: PO ↔ confirmation ↔ shipment ↔ DN ↔ GR ↔ stock ↔ inspection
    reader/        = image_recognizer (scans → claims)
    shortfall.py   = verifier/impact/shortfall.py
    timing.py      = verifier/impact/timing.py
    README.md      = verifier/README.md
  predictor/       "what will happen?"  (events + arrival forecast)
    events.py      = my impact.py (news/notice → supplier → part → product)
    cards.py       NEW: impacts.json → data/store/predictor_cards.json
  dispatcher/      "what do we do, and do it"
    cards.py render.py   = verifier/act/*
    sender.py      NEW later (Jonas): read decisions.json, send, write actions.json
  api.py feed.py   dashboard backend (Akshat, unchanged)
  cli.py           one entry: ask-soony verify | predict | dispatch | watch | ...
tests/verification/ tests/predictor/ tests/dispatcher/   (moved from verifier/**/tests)
docs/architecture.md   one diagram + the JSON contracts between the three systems
```
Data flow (files only, no cross-imports except dispatcher reading verification results):
`watcher → store` → `verification` (issues, shortfall) + `predictor` (impacts)
→ `*cards*.json` → dashboard → `decisions.json` → `dispatcher` → `actions.json`.

## Steps
0. **Prerequisite (Farhan):** rewrite `verifier` branch history to drop commit `b563d6a`
   (`data/portal/` committed); restore `data/` + `.claude/` lines in `.gitignore`.
1. Merge order: `verifier` → `akshat/dashboard` → `jonas/watcher-dashboard` → `feat/predictor`
   into a new branch `refactor/layout` (each owner agrees; announce in PROGRESS.md Now line).
2. `git mv` files into the layout above (keeps history). Pure moves in one commit.
3. Rewrite imports in a second commit: `verifier.linker` → `ask_soony.verification.linker`,
   `verifier.image_recognizer` → `ask_soony.verification.reader`,
   `verifier.impact` → `ask_soony.verification`, `verifier.act` → `ask_soony.dispatcher`,
   `ask_soony.<core mod>` → `ask_soony.core.<mod>` (~35 files, mechanical sed + ruff `--fix` for import order).
4. `pyproject.toml`: drop `pythonpath=["."]` and `verifier` testpath; testpaths = `["tests"]`;
   move per-file ruff ignores to new paths.
5. CLI: add subcommands wrapping the existing `__main__` entry points
   (`verify build|trace|issues`, `verify read`, `predict [--text]`, `dispatch`), keep
   `python -m ask_soony.verification.linker` working.
6. New small code: `predictor/cards.py` maps each impact with `launch_risk != "no"` to the
   dashboard card shape (stable id = event id); false alarms become one info card.
7. Write `docs/architecture.md`; update README, `plan.md` §4 module names.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest` (all moved tests pass, same count as before the move)
- `uv run ruff check src tests`
- `uv run ask-soony verify build` prints the same issue counts as `python -m verifier.linker build` did
- `uv run ask-soony predict --path soony/news` → magnet news "NO launch risk"
- `uv run ask-soony dispatch` writes `decision_cards.json`; `scripts/dashboard.sh` shows
  verifier + predictor cards together
- `git ls-files data/` is empty

Farhan's `verifier` (PR #2, 38 commits) is not in `main` yet. We want to run it together
with the event impact agent (`feat/predictor`) and latest `main` now, while keeping the
eventual merge to `main` easy. Catch: `verifier` commit `b563d6a` committed ~330
confidential portal files under `data/portal/` and dropped the `data/` rule from
`.gitignore`. Our integration must not carry that data into our history.

merge with **no conflicts**.

1. `git switch feat/predictor && git merge origin/main` (picks up "Add interview gaps to plan").
2. `git switch -c integration/verifier` from that.
3. `git merge --squash origin/verifier` → staged, not committed.
4. Drop the data from the squash: `git rm -r --cached -q data/` (files stay on disk, ignored).
5. Fix `.gitignore`: keep `data/` and the `soony-data/` lines; do **not** take the
   `.claude/` ignore line (it would hide the team's committed hooks). Keep the rest.

   `origin/verifier@43a8e69` and that data was excluded.

   after the Entire checks (`entire status`, `entire brain status`).

Why squash: a normal merge would pull `b563d6a` (the data) into our history and later
into `main`. The squash gives one clean commit with identical code. When Farhan merges a
cleaned `verifier` into `main`, our branch rebases on it with no or trivial conflicts
(same file contents); our squash commit then becomes empty and drops out.

- Farhan rewrites `verifier` without `b563d6a` (or squash-merges PR #2 excluding `data/`).
